name: illumwhite_illumgray
expr: iw0 = illumwhite(A,0); iw1 = illumwhite(A); iw5 = illumwhite(A,5); ig0 = illumgray(A); ig10 = illumgray(A,[10 10]); ig2n = illumgray(A,1,'Norm',2);
covers: illumgray(A, p, 'Norm', n) custom p-norm exponent
comment: Sig 1: illumwhite(A, P, 'Mask', M) — per-channel histogram thresholded at strictly more than N·P/100 pixels at-or-above. Sig 2: illumgray(A, [p_lo p_hi], 'Mask', M, 'Norm', n) — per-channel mean (or p-norm-mean) after trimming bottom p_lo% and top p_hi%. Both algorithms decompose channel-by-channel (NOT by L2 norm of RGB). Per-channel histogram-bin quantisation in MATLAB (2^16 bins for double input) adds ~1.5e-5 noise vs our direct sort, hence tol = 5e-5. The illumwhite source we inspected uses imhist quantisation; numkit sorts the raw pixel array. Both algorithms agree on which pixel is selected — they disagree only on which BIN that pixel landed in. illumgray bit-equal at machine precision because the histogram threshold is used only to pick which pixels to keep (a SET operation), not their values.
